text:
Jamie: Heads-up — starting a short RFC follow-up on the slab recomposition idea. Goal: split the runtime "hot" inference path from the colder batch/enrichment path to reduce tail latency and shrink hotpath service surface. Pinging @Sandeep @Lia for design, @Kevin for ops window.

Sandeep: SGTM. Two quick questions: who owns session metadata after split? and how do we avoid cross-service consistency problems?

Lia: My vote is Approach B — dual-write + read-fallback with a short convergence window. Minimizes blocking cutovers.

Alex: Dual-write is safe but noisy. Billing/metrics duplication is painful. Would prefer a read-proxy shim that centralizes logic and can be feature-flagged.

Maria: Observability note: we need per-tenant tail-latency histograms before/after. Canary at 1% with full tracing enabled. Also add synthetic prompts that exercise long-context paths.

Kevin: Ops proposal: 3-stage rollout. 1) extract interface & land compile-time shim; 2) deploy read-proxy sidecar behind feature flag; 3) dual-write (48h), then cohort ramp 1%->10%->50%->100%. Nightly window with on-call alerting.

Jamie: Putting a short plan here. Tradeoffs: dual-write = data movement but easiest rollback; proxy = cleaner but more risk if we mis-handle caching. We need explicit gates for: error-rate, p50/p95 tail, token cost delta.

Jamie: Rollout snippet:
```
# rollout plan
step 0: branch and feature-flag scaffolding
step 1: extract public inference API into slab-api package (compile-time)
step 2: deploy read-proxy sidecar (flagged) + enable tracing
step 3: enable dual-write to new slab for session-metadata for 48h
step 4: canary traffic 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated SLO checks
fallback: flip flag to old path, disable writes, drain new slab
```

Sandeep: KV cache invalidation is the other big rabbit. If we split services, prefix scoping and TTLs must be coordinated. I propose: namespaced keys + cache-lease TTLs + a migration invalidation event stream.

Lia: Agree on namespacing. For lease TTLs: conservative 10s for hot keys during cutover, relax after 72h stable.

Alex: For metrics duplication: emit canonical billing events from the proxy only. That solves double-counting during dual-write.

Maria: Add eval gating: run our eval suite (prompt set X) against canary responses and compare perplexity/regression thresholds before advancing. If regression > 0.5% for critical prompts, pause ramp.

Kevin: Ops checklist additions: DB migrator dry-run, background backfill job with rate limiter, circuit-breaker for new slab, rollback playbook documented in runbook. Suggest on-call + infra buddy during each ramp step.

Jamie: Ownership: propose handoff matrix in the RFC: slab-api (Eng-runtime), read-proxy (Eng-platform), migration/backfill (Eng-infra), monitoring/evals (Eng-ML + Observability).

Sandeep: Sounds good. Can we schedule a 1-hour sync to sign off on the feature flags and DB plan? I can do Wed 09:30 PST.

Alex: Wed works for me. I'll prepare the minimal proxy PoC code and the metrics plan.

Maria: I'll add the eval harness and a synthetic runner to flood test tails during canary.

Kevin: I'll book a 2-hour maintenance window immediately after canary if we need to roll forward fast.

infra-bot: Deploy pipeline queued: branch slab-api-extract -> pipeline #4128. ETA: 2026-03-20 01:22 UTC. Logs: https://ci.internal/reports/4128 :robot_face:

Jamie: Thanks all — action items: Alex PoC, Maria eval harness, Kevin ops runbook, Sandeep TTL/key namespacing doc. I'll update the RFC with a clearer sequence and gating metrics later today. :thumbsup:
